acceptance: Validation of a freshly saved configuration that includes tables without column tuning passes and the database is reused
A table whose column tuning is expected but absent from the persisted metadata is still reported as missing
Persisted column tuning for a table the expected configuration has no column tuning for is still reported as unexpected
Constraint drift stays detected through the section-hash markers
Regression tests run without a live cloud connection
context: Found 2026-10-15 during the Snowflake trial-exit smoke test: the reuse run found the tuned database but tuning validation failed with four errors (CUSTOMER, PART, PARTSUPP, SUPPLIER) and the run issued DROP DATABASE, 8 TRUNCATE and 8 COPY INTO. The Snowflake TPC-DS template has three such tables too. Fixed by PR #3012, merged 2026-10-16T00:02:10Z as 59a74fb64: `_compare_tuning_configurations` compares only column-tuned tables on both sides; missing column tuning and unexpected persisted column tuning still fail; constraints stay on section-hash markers. Offline regression tests use the shipped templates. Live confirmation is the campaign's reuse check.
description: `examples/tunings/snowflake/tpch_tuned.yaml` (and the packaged template) lists CUSTOMER, PART, PARTSUPP and SUPPLIER with no partitioning, clustering, distribution or sorting columns; their only tuning is the benchmark-wide constraint sections. `TuningMetadataManager.save_tunings` writes no rows for such tables, and `_rebuild_tunings_from_records` keeps only tables with `has_any_tuning()`, but the expected configuration passed to `validate_tunings` still contains them. `_compare_tuning_configurations` (`benchbox/core/tuning/metadata.py`) therefore always reports "Expected tuning for table '<T>' not found in database" for each of them, validation fails, and the run drops and reloads the tuned database. A tuned Snowflake database is never reused, so automatic clustering never settles between runs.
